summary:
FMLink reports that the Federal Aviation Administration is investing $870 million in airport infrastructure across the United States, framed around improving safety, convenience and family-friendly features amid rising travel demand. The Transportation Department is distributing 339 grants to airports in 44 states and two territories through the Airport Infrastructure Grants (AIG) program.

Named awards include: $289 million to Los Angeles International Airport for a new terminal access road; $50 million to Miami International Airport to reconstruct the terminal roof; $9.1 million to Akron-Canton Airport in Ohio to rehabilitate passenger bridges and reconstruct key airport facilities; $4.2 million to Juneau International Airport in Alaska to replace snow removal equipment; $3.7 million to Charleston International Airport in South Carolina for terminal expansion; and $3.5 million to Sugar Land Regional Airport in Texas for runway reconstruction.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford is quoted saying the agency is making airports safer and more convenient and is releasing grants at record speed to keep pace with growing travel demand.

The piece notes that AIG funding may be applied to airport planning, development, terminal improvements, baggage system upgrades, runway and taxiway rehabilitation, roadway and access improvements, and other safety-related infrastructure needs. FAA also published a data visualization map showing which airports received funding.

Relevance note for the workplace pipeline: this is public-sector transportation infrastructure and capital project news rather than workplace technology. It touches facilities and built-environment capital spending broadly, but contains nothing on visitor management, desk or room booking, hybrid and return-to-office policy, workplace analytics, attendance tracking, or vendor procurement review. No employee, occupancy, or workplace experience data is presented.
